text:
Nadia: quick note from a customer walkthrough — the "Hello" quickstart's dev loop doc shows `npm run dev` and a fetch to `/api/generate` but the example handler doesn't `await` the LLM call, so the page often renders blank for new users.
Omar: ah that explains the "empty output" support tickets. which file exactly?
Nadia: docs/quickstart/hello-react.md and examples/hello/web/api/generate.js. the client code does `fetch('/api/generate').then(r => r.json()).then(console.log)` and the handler does `res.send(stream)` without awaiting completion.
Peyton: oof. we should fix both: make the handler await and fix client to `const data = await res.json()` in the snippet, plus add a short checklist for first-deploy troubleshooting.
Nadia: suggested handler patch:
```js
// examples/hello/web/api/generate.js
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const out = await callRedwoodAPI(req.body);
  res.status(200).json({ output: out });
}
```
Omar: and client snippet: 
```js
const resp = await fetch('/api/generate', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({prompt}) });
const { output } = await resp.json();
setResult(output);
```
Peyton: also noticed the quickstart "first deploy" checklist misses a step about setting REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID for infra-backed deploys; newbies hit a 422 from the deploy API. let's add a one-line checklist item: "Ensure REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID is set when using infra-backed deployments."
Nadia: good catch. I'll open a single PR that updates the handler and client snippets, adds the checklist item, and includes a tiny e2e smoke (node script) that runs the client snippet against a local dev server to assert non-empty output.
Peyton: also please update the troubleshooting section: "If page shows no output, open browser console to see fetch errors and confirm handler awaits LLM call." short and actionable.
Nadia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/918 — updates snippets, adds checklist, and includes examples/ci/e2e_smoke.js that starts the dev server and does a POST to /api/generate (skips live LLM call by stubbing in CI).
qa-bot: lint-check: found 1 example client snippet missing `await` in docs/quickstart/hello-react.md (line 42).
Omar: will review the PR; can you make the e2e smoke resilient in CI by detecting placeholder tokens and stubbing the API call? we don't want flaky failures.
Nadia: yes, smoke script uses an env var `DOCS_STUB_LLM=true` in CI to bypass external calls and asserts the handler returns a non-empty string. local runs still exercise real flow.
deploy-bot: docs CI started for PR 918 (job: docs-ci)
deploy-bot: docs CI: lint passed; e2e smoke ran in stub mode and passed (duration: 1m 48s).
Peyton: LGTM. small nit: add a one-line note in the hello README about "dev hot-reload" so folks know to refresh when editing API handler files.
Nadia: added that note and pushed a tiny follow-up commit.
Omar: merging. thanks for catching this — should reduce blank-output tickets from new users.
Nadia: thanks team. opening follow-up issue to grep other examples for non-awaited async handlers and add a docs linter rule to flag them.
Peyton: filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/412 — assign to docs-squad. closing thread.
